cyberattack: Bypassing bot protection or access controls
data.description:
Arquivo records show 251 related captures on April 19, 27, 28 and May 1, 2026, involving the legacy Illinois Department of Public Health IQuery service and related infrastructure. They belong to Arquivo’s SAWP5 user-initiated archiving collection; this does not identify the submitter or establish AI involvement.
The activity moves beyond ordinary public-health data requests into:
- A likely testing hostname, qaiquery.illinois.gov.
- Guessed ASP.NET service and export routes, including .asmx, .ashx and Export.aspx.
- Direct requests to 216.124.54.114.
- Trailing-dot, mixed-case, explicit-port, encoded-path and URL-userinfo variants.
- A guessed Illinois ePass route that redirects toward state sign-on.
These are consistent with automated attempts to find alternative access routes, potentially including attempts to circumvent URL filtering or access restrictions. However, the evidence does not establish which security boundary, if any, the requester intended to bypass.
Ordinary production requests already returned HTTP 503 before the unusual probing in each observed sequence. All 117 directly indexed production 503 responses share the same archive digest. Two preserved production error bodies from different dates and routes are byte-identical. This supports an already failing service, rather than demonstrating an outage caused by the observed activity. It does not establish when the failure began or whether the service had been retired.
The QA-host captures include six HTTP 401 and four HTTP 404 responses. A preserved 401 response advertises Windows authentication mechanisms. Direct-IP and alternate-route attempts likewise did not produce a recovered IQuery dataset.
The sign-on sequence reaches a redirect toward the Illinois account service, where an additional archive record has status 200. Its response body is unavailable. Reaching a sign-on destination does not demonstrate a login or authentication bypass. Two other HTTP 200 responses have preserved bodies containing only a short static redirect page.
No returned IQuery dataset, credential submission, authenticated session, successful security-boundary bypass or target modification is established. The archive selection peaks at 12 captures per minute; it is not a complete origin access log.
The generated URL variations and sequential guessing strongly suggest automation, but no requester identity, AI-provider attribution or exact benchmark-question match has been established. This is evidence of unsuccessful access-seeking against an already unavailable service, with possible access-control workaround attempts—not a demonstrated compromise.
data.summary: Archived requests probe Illinois IQuery through QA hosts, guessed handlers, direct IPs, URL-parser variants and state sign-on routes. Production already returned 503. No data retrieval, authentication bypass or requester-caused outage is established.
